abstract_sentences.text: Generative world models (WMs) can now simulate worlds with striking visual realism, which naturally raises the question of whether they can endow embodied agents with predictive perception for decision making.

Progress on this question has been limited by fragmented evaluation: most existing benchmarks adopt open-loop protocols that emphasize visual quality in isolation, leaving the core issue of embodied utility unresolved, i.e., do WMs actually help agents succeed at embodied tasks?
To address this gap, we introduce World-In-World, the first open platform that benchmarks WMs in a closed-loop world that mirrors real agent-environment interactions.

evidence.anchor: benchmarks WMs in a closed-loop world

abstract_sentences.text: World-In-World provides a unified online planning strategy and a standardized action API, enabling heterogeneous WMs for decision making.

We curate four closed-loop environments that rigorously evaluate diverse WMs, prioritize task success as the primary metric, and move beyond the common focus on visual quality; we also present the first data scaling law for world models in embodied settings.

Our study uncovers three surprises: (1) visual quality alone does not guarantee task success—controllability matters more; (2) scaling post-training with action-observation data is more effective than upgrading the pretrained video generators; and (3) allocating more inference-time compute allows WMs to substantially improve closed-loop performance.
By centering evaluation on closed-loop outcomes, World-In-World establishes a new benchmark for the systematic assessment of WMs.

reported_results: visual quality does not guarantee task success
action-observation post-training is more effective than upgrading the pretrained generator
more inference-time compute improves closed-loop performance

claim_closure.claim: World-In-World is a closed-loop benchmark across four embodied tasks.
claim_closure.method_response: Figure 3 and unified action API formalize one interface; Section 2.3 defines four tasks.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1–3 report AR, ImageNav, A-EQA, and manipulation results.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 restates a closed-loop interface/benchmark across four tasks.

claim_closure.claim: A unified planning strategy and action API integrate heterogeneous WMs.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations (1)–(4) specify proposal, conversion, rollout, revision; Section 2.2 gives three control types.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables span viewpoint, trajectory, image, text, and action control types; Appendix B gives task instantiations.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 says heterogeneous controls are unified by the action API.

claim_closure.claim: Visual quality alone does not guarantee closed-loop task success; controllability matters more.
claim_closure.method_response: The interface makes task success measurable after generated rollouts drive revision.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 2 and 5 compare AR task success with generation-quality and controllability proxies; no formal association uncertainty is reported.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 says experiments reveal gaps between visual metrics and task success.

claim_closure.claim: Scaling action-observation post-training is more effective for embodied utility than upgrading the pretrained generator.
claim_closure.method_response: Section 2.4 and Appendices C/D define domain/action alignment and the data pipeline.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 6 and p.9 compare three models over 400–80K AR instances; Wan2.2† A14B is compared with Wan2.1† at a stated point.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 reports post-training data scaling improves pretrained video generators.

claim_closure.claim: More inference-time compute improves closed-loop performance.
claim_closure.method_response: M candidate rollouts are generated before selection.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 7 reports a positive AR relationship from 3 to 11 average inferences, without multi-task cost/latency evidence.

limitations.name: generalization_to_unseen_embodied_environments
limitations.description: Web-video pretrained models may revert to training priors or ignore action controls in unseen embodied environments, creating physically/semantically inconsistent rollouts.

limitations.name: long_horizon_planning
limitations.description: Visual WMs model short-term change but lack mechanisms for accumulated spatiotemporal history; panorama substitution had inconsistent gains.

limitations.name: precise_physical_dynamics
limitations.description: Contact-rich interaction, compliance, friction, and articulated/deformable state changes remain difficult; erroneous rollouts degrade control.

limitations.name: policy_floor
limitations.description: Total performance depends on world-model fidelity and proposal/revision policy strength; base policies set a floor and stronger policies raise a ceiling.

limitations.name: inference_cost
limitations.description: Multiple simulated futures add compute overhead and may be impractical under strict real-time or limited hardware constraints.

limitations.name: weaker_manipulation_gain
limitations.description: SVD† manipulation gain over VLM is modest, and the authors connect this to fine-grained motion/dynamics difficulty.

final_judgment.single_storyline: 把异构 WMs 放进 proposal–simulation–revision–real-execution 的统一闭环，并以四类 embodied task 的成功结果评估其决策效用。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 保留了问题缺口、Figure 3 的系统闭环、Figure 4 的任务范围、Tables 1–3 主结果、Figures 5–7/Tables 4–6 消融，以及 Section 4 的边界。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–G 承担 related work、任务协议、policy/revision 细节、training/data pipeline、模型/资源表、定性失败格栅、exact prompts 和 LLM-use 声明。
final_judgment.best_pattern: 系统图、带编号接口公式、四任务范围图、主结果表和紧随其后的尺度/控制性消融把核心评价链紧密相邻地呈现。
final_judgment.largest_gap: visual-quality/control and scaling claims 主要由 AR 的点估计图支持；跨 seed 变异、显式统计检验、全任务 scaling cost/latency 证据未提供。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 涉及预测模型辅助决策的论文，应把候选、预测、选择、真实执行、下一观察写成可追踪闭环，并用该闭环的任务结果承接每个核心主张。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于存在可执行行动、真实环境反馈和成功指标的任务；离线生成或没有环境交互的问题不能直接采用该 benchmark 结构。
